chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It was said to him, 'What is the matter with the companions of Jesus (peace be upon him) that they used to walk on water, while this is not the case with the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said, 'Indeed, the companions of Jesus (peace be upon him) were made sufficient [by God] in their livelihood, but these [companions of Muhammad] were tested with livelihood.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the companions of Jesus walk on water but the companions of Muhammad did not?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contrasts the spiritual states of the disciples of Jesus (AS) and Muhammad (SAW) by linking their miraculous signs to their relationship with material sustenance (*ma'ash*). While the former were granted divine sufficiency, allowing miracles to manifest as supernatural elevation like walking on water, the latter are tested through the mundane pursuit of livelihood, transforming daily economic struggle into a profound act of worship and spiritual refinement.
